evals.name: Validate a bug fix through the integration harness
evals.prompt: Build MID-123: 'Model hydration crashes when optional fields are null instead of missing. Expected: null fields treated same as missing — defaults applied. Validation errors for required fields must be preserved.' ModelHydration.integration.test.ts exercises the real parser-to-hydrator boundary.
evals.expected_output: The agent reproduces the failure through the integration harness, implements the minimal fix, reruns the harness and relevant checks, and reports the evidence. No scope creep.
assertions: Uses the integration harness as the primary behavior evidence
Reproduces the null-field failure through the real boundary
Implementation is minimal
The integration harness passes after the fix
Existing validation behavior is preserved

evals.name: Validate interface behavior through the UI harness
evals.prompt: Build MID-124: 'Disable Save while the profile request is in flight and show the API error inline.' Component unit tests exist, and the repository has a UI test harness that renders the real form with its request adapter.
evals.expected_output: The agent implements the smallest change and validates loading and error behavior through the existing UI harness rather than relying only on mocked component logic.
assertions: Selects the existing UI harness
Validates the disabled Save state
Validates the inline API error
Does not add an end-to-end test when the UI harness proves the boundary

evals.name: Treat intentional behavior drift as an unauthorized rescope
evals.prompt: Build MID-789: 'Gracefully degrade when malformed payloads arrive — return partial model with warnings.' During implementation, you conclude strict rejection would be better because silent degradation has been hiding data bugs for months, but the ticket has not been updated and the operator has not authorized the behavior change.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs an intent check, identifies strict rejection as a behavior divergence from the canonical acceptance criteria, and stops for a focused rescope decision rather than treating intention as authorization.
assertions: References the original graceful-degradation acceptance criterion
Classifies strict rejection as a behavior or scope divergence
Does not silently implement the divergent behavior
Requests authorization to rescope with one focused question

evals.name: Detect accidental scope creep and escalate
evals.prompt: Build MID-456: 'Add a cancel button to the model edit form.' While building, you realize you've also refactored the entire form validation system because it seemed related. The ticket didn't ask for that.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs an intent drift check, identifies the form validation refactor as accidental scope creep, and escalates with a focused question about whether to reduce scope or keep the refactor.
assertions: Runs an intent drift check
Identifies the form validation refactor as outside ticket scope
Classifies it as accidental scope creep
Escalates to the operator with a focused question

evals.name: Skip continuity and learning artifacts for completed trivial work
evals.prompt: Build this trivial task: fix a typo in one README heading. No behavior changes, no remaining work, and no reusable learning.
evals.expected_output: The agent makes the change, performs a targeted check, and finishes without creating session-state or compound artifacts and without narrating no-op ceremony.
assertions: Treats the change as trivial
Runs a targeted check
Creates no session-state artifact
Creates no learning artifact
Does not emit a Done/Left/Blocked template

evals.name: Capture learning only when it passes the admission test
evals.prompt: Build MID-567: 'Fix the race condition in concurrent model saves.' After implementing with an optimistic lock, you discover a previously undocumented repository-wide rule: all save paths bypass concurrency control, the same bug exists in three modules, and rediscovering the affected paths required a long trace.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the learning as novel, reusable beyond the ticket, and expensive to rediscover, then proposes or writes one durable repository learning without a raw per-Build capture.
assertions: Applies all three learning admission criteria
Uses one durable destination
Does not create a raw continuous-compound artifact
Keeps the Build result concise
